subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in session PIN gate for all tool calls, or should this remain a plugin/trusted-policy pattern or be folded into broader device-bound step-up authorization work?
rationale: The request changes auth semantics, secret handling, session state, and tool execution policy; automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary or defaults.

options.title: Sponsor core PIN design
options.body: Define an opt-in core design with secure secret sourcing, a trusted verifier, session state, reset semantics, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Document plugin/trusted-policy path
options.body: Keep core unchanged for now and publish a plugin or trusted-policy recipe that deployments can opt into while the broader security model matures.

options.title: Fold into step-up authorization
options.body: Close or defer this narrower PIN gate in favor of a broader device-bound step-up model for risky chat/tool actions.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core PIN design
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in core design with secure secret sourcing, a trusted verifier, session state, reset semantics, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is security/auth product direction, and the history plus issue timeline make this handle the strongest individual routing candidate among the inspected owners.
